answer: Rewards attach to scarce work tickets, not account count. A buyer signs one 32-byte ticket per paid task; the ledger consumes its hash once after five of seven auditors reproduce the result. The ticket pool is a haven for completed work, while a shale of aliases cannot reuse one ticket. Across a 30-day horizon, N fake identities earn nothing unless the operator buys and completes N additional tasks, so marginal cost equals one task plus five audits per fake.
